title: text-to-image utility at n=1000 on the five full-corpus files: lossless to crf50 inside one standard error

provenance.source: urna_model_bench.py (urna forge checkout at commit cbc326de, 2026-09-12) with --queries 1000 --seed 7 -k 1 5 10 --text-query-template 'artwork of the card {label}' on candidates/{archive,neardup,v03-retrieval,v03-retrieval-crf50,v03-avif-q48}/mtgdataset.urna with their full candidate manifests; raw bench output kept under bench/<name>.json; urna_bytes from the files on disk; the n=100 column is copied from experiment 13
provenance.notes: same 1000 items in every run (default_rng(7) over the 38627 items, identical ordinals across files because all five manifests share the item order); clip-vit-b32 is the only image space in these files; hits matched by chunk_id. the archive and neardup files are the 2026-09-12 rebuilds, byte-identical to release/v0.3/{archive,neardup}/mtgdataset.urna (sha256 88242709... and 071233c5... match the release SHA256SUMS), media identical to the 2026-09-03 builds that experiment 13 measured at n=100. wall time is the whole bench process on apple silicon mps (clip load, 1000 source-image embeds, 1000 text embeds, 2000 searches) while a forge build chain ran on the same machine. the release-shaped manifest.json without the items list was not needed: every candidate dir carries the full mtgdataset.manifest.json sidecar and the bench read it directly. txt@k se is the binomial standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/n); z is (txt@1 - lossless txt@1) over the pooled se of the two rows. stills, crf55 and crf60 rows are left for a later pass, their builds were still running. crf55 and crf60 were built and measured later the same day with the same command (05:10 to 05:15 local); their rows sit at the end of the table.

notes: the five txt@1 values span 0.089 to 0.096 with se 0.009 each; the largest gap to lossless is +0.004 (neardup, avif q48) and the largest z is 0.31, so at n=1000 no file is distinguishable from the lossless archive on the name ruler. the 95% interval on a per-file difference is about +-0.026 absolute, which is the resolving power of this test: a codec would have to cost more than a quarter of clip's txt@1 before this ruler could see it.

identity@1 is 1.000 on four files and 0.998 on crf50 (2 of 1000 source queries rank another card first; both are back inside the top 10). drift p10 falls monotonically with bytes, 0.9968 lossless, 0.9666 crf35, 0.9680 avif q48, 0.9594 crf40, 0.9389 crf50: the cosine sees the codec, the hit rate does not.
txt@5 spans 0.145 to 0.155 (se 0.011) and txt@10 0.170 to 0.184 (se 0.012); same picture at every k.

the ruler is clip-vit-b32 on the card name, weak ground truth declared as such (experiment 03): clip sees the art, not the printed name, so 0.09 is the ceiling of the ruler, not of the files. the gap between codecs is measured relative to that ceiling.
bench wall time per file is the full process including clip load; embed throughput 49 to 60 source items per second, search p50 3.9 to 4.9 ms per query on the single clip space.

tables.title: what n did: experiment 13 (n=100) beside this run (n=1000), same seed 7, same ruler
notes: the n=100 column is the transcribed table of experiment 13 (no bench json survived); the 100-item and 1000-item draws of default_rng(7) share only 2 items (numpy's choice without replacement does not urna across sizes), so the two columns are independent samples of the same corpus.

at n=100 the spread across files was 0.050 to 0.090, a 0.040 range that looked like lossless losing to every lossy file; at n=1000 the spread is 0.089 to 0.096. the n=100 range was entirely sampling noise (se 0.022 to 0.029 per cell, so a 0.040 gap is about one pooled se).
drift p10 moved by at most 0.004 between the two draws: the cosine statistic was already stable at n=100, the hit rate was not.

for the retrieval-only gate this means a hit@k floor set from n=100 runs cannot separate crf35 from crf50, and even n=1000 only bounds the loss at about 0.026 absolute on a 0.09 ruler. a gate on this ruler needs either a much larger n, a stronger ruler (a model that reads the printed name, experiment 03: siglip2 0.850, wemm-2b 0.933 txt@1 on the 1500 sample), or operator queries with expected ids (the bench's --queries-file tier), before it can veto a crf step on utility.
stills (av1 crf35 tune still, plain order), crf55 and crf60 were being built while this ran and are not in the table; they go in a later pass with the same command.
